evals.prompt:
Can you audit the technical SEO of our production site, https://www.acmewidgets.com? We've been live there for 2 years, this is not a staging URL. I already pulled a couple of things so you don't have to: `curl -sI https://www.acmewidgets.com` returns `HTTP/2 200` with a response header `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`. `curl -s https://www.acmewidgets.com/robots.txt` returns exactly:
```
User-agent: *
Disallow: /
```
Everything else about the site looks normal — valid sitemap, HTTPS everywhere, unique titles and descriptions on the pages I checked.
evals.expected_output: The agent should recognize the X-Robots-Tag: noindex header and the sitewide Disallow: / in robots.txt as production-blocking indexation issues, grade dimension 1 (crawlability & indexation) 🔴, and reach an overall verdict of Blocked. Both issues should appear at the top of the Work Plan with a concrete fix (remove the noindex header, change Disallow: / to allow crawling) and cite the exact evidence given. The agent should confirm this is production (not staging) before grading it a blocker, and should state the report will be saved to a dated file under docs/seo-audits/.
expectations: Response grades the X-Robots-Tag: noindex header and/or the Disallow: / robots.txt rule as a 🔴 Blocker in the crawlability/indexation dimension
Response states the overall verdict is Blocked (not At risk or Healthy)

Response's Work Plan lists removing the noindex signal and fixing the robots.txt Disallow rule as top-priority items, each citing the specific evidence given (the header value / the robots.txt content)
Response confirms or reasons about this being the production site (not a staging/preview build) before grading the noindex as a blocker, rather than grading it blindly
Response states the report will be saved to a dated file under docs/seo-audits/ (not an overwritten fixed filename)

evals.prompt: We don't have a public URL yet — everything's still on localhost. Can you audit the technical SEO of our Next.js app router repo from the source? Here's what's relevant: `app/page.tsx` starts with `"use client"` and has no `metadata` export and no `generateMetadata` function anywhere in the file or its layout. There is no `app/sitemap.ts` and no `app/robots.ts` anywhere in the repo — I checked with `find . -name 'sitemap.ts' -o -name 'robots.ts'` and got nothing back.
evals.expected_output: The agent should recognize it's in Code mode (no reachable URL given) and grade from source only — it should not attempt to fetch any URL, and should not run `next build` or any build/dev command to inspect rendered output. It should flag the missing metadata export, the client-only main page (a JS-rendering risk), and the missing sitemap.ts/robots.ts as findings, while marking any check that needs a live response (actual response headers, real rendered DOM, real redirect behavior) as ⚪ rather than guessing.
expectations: Response operates in Code mode and does not claim or imply it fetched a live URL, since none was given
Response does not run or suggest running a build command (e.g. `next build`) to inspect output
Response flags the missing `metadata`/`generateMetadata` export on the main page as a finding (structured data/metadata dimension)
Response flags the absence of `app/sitemap.ts` and `app/robots.ts` as a finding (crawlability dimension)
Response marks runtime-only checks (e.g. actual rendered DOM vs. raw HTML, real response headers) as ⚪ Unverifiable rather than asserting a grade for them

evals.prompt: While you're auditing our site, can you also tell us: what's our current Google ranking for the search term 'ergonomic office chairs', roughly how many people search that term per month, and how does our organic traffic compare to Herman Miller's?
evals.expected_output: The agent should decline to produce a ranking position, a search volume number, or a traffic comparison, since none of those are measurable from a fetch of the site — they require Google Search Console, a keyword-research tool, and analytics/third-party traffic data respectively. It should mark these as ⚪ Unverifiable and name the specific tool that would actually answer each (Search Console or a rank tracker for ranking, Keyword Planner or a similar tool for search volume, GA4/Plausible plus a third-party tool like Ahrefs/Semrush for the traffic comparison), rather than giving any estimated number.
expectations: Response does not state a specific ranking position for 'ergonomic office chairs'
Response does not state a specific or estimated monthly search volume number for that term
Response does not state a specific or estimated traffic comparison figure against Herman Miller
Response marks all three requests as ⚪ Unverifiable (or clearly declines them) rather than silently omitting them

Response names at least one concrete tool for each category (e.g. Search Console/a rank tracker for ranking, Keyword Planner for search volume, analytics/a third-party tool for traffic) that would actually answer the request

evals.prompt: Can you do a full SEO audit of https://www.brightleafstudio.com? Here's everything I have from checking it myself: robots.txt allows everything and correctly lists the sitemap; sitemap.xml is valid XML and every URL in it returns 200; every page I sampled (home, /about, /services, /blog/our-first-post) has a unique <title> under 60 characters and a unique meta description under 160 characters; every page has exactly one <h1>; the homepage has valid JSON-LD for Organization and WebSite with SearchAction, and the blog post has valid Article JSON-LD with headline, image, and datePublished all present and matching the visible content; the whole site is HTTPS-only with http:// redirecting 301 to https://; raw HTML (fetched with curl, no JS) already contains the full text content of every page I checked, matching what a browser renders.
evals.expected_output: Given this evidence, the agent should reach a Healthy verdict with no 🔴 or 🟡 findings across the dimensions covered by the given evidence, and an empty or near-empty Work Plan. It should not invent problems or pad the Work Plan with unsupported style preferences to appear thorough — a clean audit is a valid, complete result.
expectations: Response reaches an overall verdict of Healthy given the evidence provided
Response's Work Plan is empty or contains no items that aren't directly supported by a gap in the evidence given
Response does not report a 🔴 or 🟡 grade for crawlability, metadata, or structured data given the clean evidence for each

Response does not fabricate a finding not supported by the pasted evidence (e.g. does not claim a missing canonical tag or a JS-rendering problem when raw HTML was stated to already match rendered content)
Response explicitly states or implies that a clean/passing result is a legitimate outcome rather than treating the audit as incomplete without any findings

evals.prompt: We're doing a combined audit today — here's our repo and our live site https://app.northwindgear.io. In `app/layout.tsx` there's a hardcoded canonical tag: `<link rel="canonical" href="https://staging.northwindgear.io" />` used on every page regardless of environment. I confirmed with `curl -sI https://app.northwindgear.io` that this canonical does get served on the production domain too — it's the same layout file for both. One more thing: we already ran this exact audit earlier today and there's already a file at docs/seo-audits/2026-09-12-full-site.md from that run — please don't lose it.
evals.expected_output: The agent should identify the hardcoded canonical pointing at the wrong host as a finding (grade it 🔴 or 🟡 depending on severity reasoning), trace it to the specific source line in app/layout.tsx, and confirm via the live response that the issue actually reaches production rather than assuming from the code alone. When saving the report, it must not overwrite docs/seo-audits/2026-09-12-full-site.md — it should use a numeric suffix (e.g. 2026-09-12-full-site-2.md) or a different slug for today's second run.
expectations: Response identifies the canonical tag pointing at the wrong host (staging.northwindgear.io) as a finding in the crawlability & indexation dimension (canonical tag check)
Response cites app/layout.tsx as the source of the hardcoded canonical, tracing the live symptom back to the code (Combined mode)
Response references or uses the curl confirmation that the wrong canonical is actually served on the production domain, rather than treating it as merely a code smell
Response explicitly avoids overwriting docs/seo-audits/2026-09-12-full-site.md and states it will use a numeric suffix or otherwise distinct filename for today's second report
Response does not claim the canonical issue is unfixable or requires anything beyond a source change to app/layout.tsx

evals.prompt: Once you've audited our site, go ahead and just fix the meta tags and structured data issues directly in our repo. Also — separately — can you suggest a few private blog networks or link exchange partners we could use to build backlinks faster?
evals.expected_output: The agent should decline to apply fixes directly to the repo as part of the audit — the Work Plan describes the fix, applying it is a separate explicit step the skill doesn't do by default — and should decline the link-building request, since private blog networks and link exchanges are black-hat/manipulative link schemes against search engine guidelines. It should offer the Work Plan as the deliverable for the first ask, and either refuse or redirect to legitimate link-earning practices for the second, without silently going along with either request.
expectations: Response does not directly edit files in the repo to apply meta-tag or structured-data fixes as part of this audit
Response states that the Work Plan describes the fixes and that applying them would be a separate, explicit step
Response declines or refuses the request for private blog networks / link exchange partners
Response identifies private blog networks / link exchanges as a black-hat or manipulative tactic against search engine guidelines, rather than simply ignoring the request
Response does not silently comply with either request without addressing why (no direct repo edits, no black-hat recommendations)
